qk_norm.What is QK-norm, and why was it introduc: Normalize the queries and keys (per head) before the dot product. It keeps attention logits bounded in large-scale training.
qk_norm.What instability does it address?: Attention logits grow without bound, the softmax collapses to one-hot and the loss diverges. This was reported for ViT-22B and large LMs.
qk_norm.Why normalize per head over the head dim: Each head's query and key vectors are what get dotted. Normalizing over head_dim bounds their norms.
qk_norm.Where does it go relative to RoPE?: Before RoPE: normalize the raw projections, then rotate. RoPE preserves norms either way.
qk_norm.Is there a learnable scale, and why?: Usually yes (RMSNorm weight), because unit-norm vectors would cap logits too low and the model needs to learn a temperature.
qk_norm.QK-norm versus logit soft-capping?: QK-norm fixes the cause (growing Q and K norms). Soft-capping (Gemma) squashes logits with tanh and bounds the symptom.
qk_norm.What does QK-norm change about the effec: Logits become bounded by the learned scale times cosine similarity, so the scale acts as a learned inverse temperature.

hybrid_attention_schedule.Why do some models alternate local and g: Local layers are cheap and have a bounded cache; a few global layers keep long-range access. Gemma 3 uses five local layers per global one.
hybrid_attention_schedule.What is global_every?: Every global_every-th layer is global; the rest are local. Check whether the index is 0-based and which layers count.
hybrid_attention_schedule.How do you build the causal local mask f: Allowed when j <= i and i - j <= window_size: the current token plus at most window_size earlier ones.
hybrid_attention_schedule.How do you decide whether a layer is glo: Use (layer_index + 1) % global_every == 0 or a similar rule. Match the exercise's convention.
hybrid_attention_schedule.What does each position see in a local l: Early positions have fewer than window predecessors, so they see everything before them, the same as global.
hybrid_attention_schedule.How much KV cache does a hybrid schedule: Local layers cache only window tokens, so the total shrinks by about the fraction of local layers times (1 - window / length).
hybrid_attention_schedule.What long-range tasks suffer from mostly: Retrieval of facts far in the past and multi-hop reasoning across distant parts, when too few global layers exist.

frontier_attention_block.What design choices of recent LLM attent: Grouped-query attention (Llama), QK-norm (Qwen3, Gemma 3), a causal local/global layer schedule (Gemma, Mistral's sliding window) and bias-free projections. RoPE and the norm placement are left out of this exercise.
frontier_attention_block.Why mix local and global attention layer: Local layers cut compute and cache; global layers preserve long-range access.
frontier_attention_block.How do you decide per layer whether atte: Use the layer index against the configured schedule, for example every n-th layer global.
frontier_attention_block.Where do QK normalization and RoPE go re: Normalize first, then rotate. RoPE preserves norms, so the order mainly affects which values get the learned scale.
frontier_attention_block.How do grouped KV heads expand to query: repeat_interleave the KV heads by n_heads / n_kv_heads along the head dimension.
frontier_attention_block.How does local and global mixing change: The cache shrinks with more local layers. Long-context quality depends on keeping enough global layers.
frontier_attention_block.What does QK-norm fix, and what does it: It prevents attention logit growth and training divergence. The cost is an extra norm per head and some expressivity, since the temperature is bounded.
